blocks.instruction: Leia o texto e escolha a alternativa correta. Algumas perguntas pedem inferência — a resposta não está escrita com todas as letras.
blocks.passage:
Not everything you receive is taxed. Taxable income is the money the tax office counts when it decides what you owe. Salaries, business profits, rental income, and most investments are taxable.

Non-taxable income is money that, by law, is left out. Some gifts, some scholarships, and certain benefits are not taxed. There are a few other exceptions too.

The rules are not the same in every country, and they change over time. But the idea is always the same. The tax office draws a line: everything on one side is counted, and everything on the other side is not. Knowing which side each amount sits on is the first real skill of doing a tax return well.

items.q: What is taxable income?
options: Money the tax office counts when it decides what you owe
Money that is always left out
items.why: "Taxable income is the money the tax office counts when it decides what you owe."

items.q: Which of these is NON-taxable, according to the text?
items.why: "Some gifts, some scholarships, and certain benefits are not taxed."

items.q: The text says the rules…
options: are the same in every country
are not the same in every country, and they change
items.why: "The rules are not the same in every country, and they change over time."

items.q: The text suggests that doing a tax return correctly…
options: starts with knowing what is taxable and what is not
items.why: Inferência: "Knowing which side each amount sits on is the first real skill" — é o ponto de partida.

items.q: The author would most likely DISAGREE with this idea:
options: The rules can change over time
Every amount you receive is always taxed
You should know which income is taxable
items.why: Inferência: o texto começa dizendo "Not everything you receive is taxed", então nem tudo é tributado.

blocks.instruction: Ouça Charlotte explicando a lista de rendas para o novo assistente. Responda sem ler a transcrição — ela só aparece depois de corrigir.

audio.text:
Okay, let's go through the client's list together. Before we prepare the tax return, we must sort each income. Is it taxable, or is it not? That is the first step.

Look at the first line. This is the client's salary. A salary is taxable, so we count it. Next line: rental income from an apartment. That is taxable too. And here, business profit from her small shop — also taxable. We add all three.

Now look at this one. Her son received a scholarship for university. In this case, that scholarship is not taxable, so we leave it out. And this gift from her mother — it is a small gift, and it is not taxed here. So we leave it out as well.

Please be careful. The rules can change, and they are not the same in every country. So never guess. When you are not sure, check the tax office rules, or ask me. Getting this split right is the most important part of the job. If we count the wrong income, the whole return is wrong.
audio.label: Ouça quantas vezes precisar. A transcrição aparece depois de corrigir.

items.q: What is the first step, according to Charlotte?
options: Sort each income as taxable or not
items.why: "Before we prepare the tax return, we must sort each income. Is it taxable, or is it not? That is the first step."

items.q: Which incomes does Charlotte count as taxable?
options: The salary, the rental income, and the business profit
items.why: "A salary is taxable… rental income… also taxable. And here, business profit… also taxable. We add all three."

items.q: Why does Charlotte leave the scholarship out?
options: Because it is not taxable in this case
Because the son did not receive it
items.why: "that scholarship is not taxable, so we leave it out."

items.q: Charlotte says "never guess." What does this suggest?
options: The client already knows the answer
The assistant should check the rules when not sure
items.why: Inferência: ela pede para checar as regras da receita ou perguntar quando houver dúvida.

items.q: Why is getting the split right so important?
options: Because if the wrong income is counted, the whole return is wrong
Because the client pays more that way
Because the tax office prefers it
items.why: Inferência: "If we count the wrong income, the whole return is wrong."

blocks.instruction: O vocabulário da lição aparece aqui em frases novas. Escolha o sentido ou a palavra que cabe no contexto.

items.q: "Her salary is paid at the end of every month." A salary is…
options: the money you receive for your work
items.why: Salary = salário: o dinheiro que você recebe pelo trabalho.

items.q: Choose the correct word: "He owns two apartments, so he has ___ every month."
items.why: Rental income = renda de aluguel, o dinheiro que vem dos imóveis alugados.

items.q: "The tax office sent her a letter about the return." The tax office is…
options: the government body that deals with taxes
items.why: Tax office = receita: o órgão do governo que cuida dos impostos.

items.q: Choose the correct word: "Her son won a ___ to study at the university for free."
items.why: Scholarship = bolsa de estudos, para estudar sem pagar.

items.q: "There is one exception to this rule." An exception is…
options: a case that does not follow the normal rule
items.why: Exception = exceção: um caso que foge da regra normal.

blocks.instruction: Expressões que aparecem no trabalho de contabilidade e impostos. Escolha o sentido no contexto.

items.q: "The manager must sign off on the tax return before we send it." To sign off on means to…
items.why: Sign off on = aprovar formalmente, dar o aval.

items.q: "Let's go through the list one line at a time." To go through means to…
items.why: Go through = revisar com cuidado, item por item.

items.q: "We leave out the non-taxable income." To leave out means to…
items.why: Leave out = deixar de fora, não incluir.

items.q: "Please fill in the form with the correct numbers." To fill in means to…
items.why: Fill in = preencher com as informações.

items.q: "If you are not sure, check with the tax office." To check with someone means to…
items.why: Check with = confirmar com alguém, perguntar para ter certeza.
